summary: SIMEC Atlantis Energy (now SAE Renewables) announced in 2019 a 'world's first ocean-powered' hyperscale data centre in Caithness, supplied by private wire from an expanded MeyGen tidal array, targeting operation by 2024. An EIA screening request for a data centre at Mey (20/01258/SCRE) was decided by Highland Council in March 2020, but no application followed and the original timeline lapsed. The 20+ ha SAE-owned greenfield site is now marketed by Invest Highland as an investment opportunity; SAE's current planning activity at Mey is a 300 MW battery storage scheme.
maturity_explanation: A real early-development step is evidenced: EIA screening request 20/01258/SCRE for 'Development of data centre' at Land 500m West of Philips Mains, Mey, decided 2020-03-25 — consistent in place and timing with the SIMEC Atlantis MeyGen data centre announcement. No planning application, PAN or scoping has followed in six years; the site is now marketed as an opportunity, so M1 reflects the highest evidenced stage of a currently dormant proposal.

latest_development.headline: No data centre planning activity since the March 2020 EIA screening; site remains on Invest Highland's opportunity listing while SAE pursues a 300 MW BESS nearby at Mey
